Status: DRAFT

An analysis runs only after a person has read this file and approved it. Edit anything;
approval is what freezes it. After approval the plan is the record of intent -- change of
mind means a new analysis, not a quiet edit.

## Goal
Compare the two conditions, `a` and `b`, across the consensus peak set, in both assays this
project ran: ATAC-seq (`atacseq_bulk`, 1324 consensus peaks) and ChIP-seq (`chipseq_bulk`,
antibody `ab-a`, 1472 consensus peaks).
For each assay independently, test every consensus peak for a difference in read counts
between condition `b` and condition `a`, and return a ranked, per-peak table of effect sizes
and adjusted p-values, plus the diagnostic plots needed to judge whether that ranking is
trustworthy.
The contrast is **b vs a** throughout, with `a` as the reference level, so a positive
log2 fold change means more signal in condition `b`.
This analysis reports the statistics; what the changed peaks mean biologically is not in
scope.

## Inputs
Artifact types resolve through each sub-stage's OUTPUTS.tsv at execution time; the paths
below are what they resolve to today.

| Artifact type | Resolved from | Path |
|---|---|---|
| `counts_peaks` | `atacseq_bulk` / `01_nfcore-atacseq-wrapper` | `02_bioinformatics/atacseq_bulk/01_nfcore-atacseq-wrapper/run/results/bwa/merged_library/macs2/narrow_peak/consensus/consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.featureCounts.txt` |
| `peaks_consensus` | `atacseq_bulk` / `01_nfcore-atacseq-wrapper` | `02_bioinformatics/atacseq_bulk/01_nfcore-atacseq-wrapper/run/results/bwa/merged_library/macs2/narrow_peak/consensus/consensus_peaks.mLb.clN.bed` |
| `counts_peaks` | `chipseq_bulk` / `01_nfcore-chipseq-wrapper` | `02_bioinformatics/chipseq_bulk/01_nfcore-chipseq-wrapper/run/results/bwa/merged_library/macs3/broad_peak/consensus/ab-a/ab-a.consensus_peaks.featureCounts.txt` |
| `design` | `01_prepare_samplesheets` | `01_samplesheets/atacseq_bulk_design.csv` |
| `design` | `01_prepare_samplesheets` | `01_samplesheets/chipseq_bulk_design.csv` |

Every path above is opened **read-only**. Nothing under `00_data/`, `01_samplesheets/` or
`02_bioinformatics/` is modified, moved or repaired by this analysis.

Note on the ChIP `peaks_consensus` artifact: it resolves to a *directory*
(`.../macs3/broad_peak/consensus`) that contains only the featureCounts table -- there is no
consensus BED file for the ChIP assay, unlike ATAC. Peak coordinates for ChIP therefore come
from the `Chr`/`Start`/`End`/`Length` columns of its featureCounts table, which carry the same
information. No BED is synthesised and the missing one is not treated as an error.

## Method
All steps run in the `gars-bio` environment, via `$GARS_PY`
(`$GARS_BIO/bin/python`), which provides pydeseq2 0.5.4, pandas 3.0.5, numpy 2.5.2,
scipy 1.18.0 and matplotlib 3.11.1. Nothing is installed. One script,
`scripts/compare_conditions.py`, runs the whole method for both assays; a second script,
`scripts/run.sh`, is what the executor submits.

1. **Read the design.** For each assay, read its `*_design.csv` and build a
   `sample_id -> condition` map. For `chipseq_bulk`, drop the rows whose `condition` is
   `input` (`input-a-r1`, `input-a-r2`): input controls are not a biological condition and are
   not part of the b-vs-a contrast. They are already absent from the ChIP consensus count
   matrix; the script asserts that rather than assuming it.

2. **Read the count matrix and map columns to samples by NAME, never by position.** The
   featureCounts header names each count column by its BAM filename
   (`<sample>_REP<n>.mLb.clN.sorted.bam`); parse `<sample>` and `REP<n>` out of that filename
   and join to the design on `group` + `replicate`.
   *This is load-bearing.* The two matrices do not agree on column order: ATAC's columns are in
   design order (`atac-a_REP1, atac-a_REP2, atac-b_REP1, atac-b_REP2`), but ChIP's are
   **`chip-a_REP2, chip-b_REP1, chip-b_REP2, chip-a_REP1`** -- scrambled. A script that assumed
   position would be correct on ATAC and silently mislabel three of four ChIP samples,
   inverting the contrast. The script fails loudly if any count column cannot be matched to a
   design row, or if either condition ends up with fewer than 2 samples.

3. **Assemble the counts.** Index peaks by `Geneid` (`Interval_N`), keep the
   `Chr`/`Start`/`End`/`Length` columns aside as peak annotation, and build an integer counts
   frame. Transpose to **samples x peaks**, which is the orientation pydeseq2 requires, with a
   metadata frame indexed by the same sample labels carrying the `condition` column as an
   ordered categorical with `a` as the reference level.

4. **Pre-filter.** Drop peaks whose summed count across all four samples is `< 10`
   (49 of 1324 peaks in ATAC, 47 of 1472 in ChIP). This removes peaks that cannot support a
   dispersion estimate; it is applied identically to both assays and the dropped peaks are
   listed in the report, not discarded silently.

5. **Fit and test.** Per assay, `DeseqDataSet(counts=..., metadata=..., design="~condition")`,
   then `dds.deseq2()` -- median-of-ratios size factors, gene-wise dispersion estimation, the
   parametric trend fit and dispersion shrinkage. Then
   `DeseqStats(dds, contrast=["condition", "b", "a"], alpha=0.05)` and `.summary()`: a Wald
   test per peak, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR, and pydeseq2's independent filtering. Also compute
   shrunken effect sizes with `.lfc_shrink(coeff="condition[T.b]")` and report them alongside
   the unshrunken ones -- with two replicates per condition, the raw log2 fold change of a
   low-count peak is unstable and the shrunken value is the one to rank on.

6. **Annotate and write.** Join each result table back to its peak coordinates, add an `is_MT`
   flag (7 mitochondrial peaks in ATAC, 14 in ChIP -- 0.5% and 1.2% of reads respectively),
   sort by adjusted p-value then by absolute shrunken log2 fold change, and write one TSV per
   assay. **Mitochondrial peaks are flagged, not dropped** -- whether to exclude them is a
   scientific call, and this plan does not make it on your behalf; the flag lets you filter
   after the fact without a re-run.

7. **Diagnostics.** Per assay, from the size-factor-normalized counts:
   an MA plot (mean normalized count vs shrunken log2FC, points at FDR < 0.05 highlighted) and
   a PCA of log2(normalized + 1) counts over the top 500 most variable peaks, coloured by
   condition. These are how you judge whether the two replicates in each condition agree
   before believing any ranking.

8. **Summarise.** Write `results/summary.md`: per assay, the peaks tested and filtered, library
   sizes, size factors, the count significant at FDR < 0.05 and < 0.1, the direction split, the

# Genomics Agentic Research System (GARS)

A workspace for running genomics research projects through dialogue with an LLM agent. The
filesystem is the architecture; the agent is the navigator. Built on the Interpretable Context
Methodology (ICM — Van Clief & McDermott, arXiv:2603.16021), with bioinformatics executed by
nf-core pipelines through GARS-authored
wrappers — every assay's sub-stage runs on one (decisions 0028-0031).

> **Scope of this file.** Orientation for *using* a GARS workspace. If you are developing GARS
> itself — editing contracts, docs or the template — the entry point is the `CLAUDE.md` at the
> root of the GARS source repository, not this one.

## Agent entry point

Before responding to any request: read `CONTEXT.md` for the stage map, then read the `CONTEXT.md`
of the stage the request maps to. Execute that contract literally.

- Its **Scope Boundaries** are binding. Do not read, search, or act outside them, however helpful
  the deviation would seem.
- Its **Response Format** templates are the only messages to send. Add no observations,
  suggestions, or offers of work. One exception: a direct user question may be answered from
  the workspace's own files, read-only, before restating the current wait point — the bounded
  voice rule in `_references/contract_standard.md`.
- If a step appears to need deviation, stop and ask. Never act first and report afterwards.

## Where things live

| Path | Holds | Layer |
|---|---|---|
| `CONTEXT.md` | stage map, how stages connect, directory ownership | L1 |
| `00_initialize_project/` … `03_custom_analysis/` | one contract per stage; the numbering is the order | L2 |
| `02_bioinformatics/<Assay ID>/<NN_name>/` | one contract per sub-stage of an assay | L2 |
| `_references/` | domain knowledge shared by every project — assay map, artifact vocabulary, config schema, runtime | L3 |
| `_templates/` | the stamps stages copy; `project/` is the shape of a new project | L3 |
| `_system/` | `gars-env.sh` (the execution environment), the stage helpers that compute deterministic artifacts, the index builder | L3 |
| `projects/` | the work: one directory per project, plus a generated `_index.md` | L4 |
